item.title: Module: KAFKA
item.description:
Kafka is a distributed event-streaming platform. Pigsty’s KAFKA module installs Apache Kafka 4.1+ dynamic KRaft clusters on managed nodes from RPM/DEB packages. It manages security, resources, lifecycle, and observability.

Current status: Beta module

Kafka is a Beta module. Before production use, test it thoroughly and verify that it meets your requirements. Test dynamic KRaft, strict rolling restarts, TLS/SCRAM/ACL, declared topics and users, credential and certificate rotation, and the complete monitoring pipeline.

item.title: Quick Start
item.description:
First build a single-node cluster, create a topic, and read and write messages. Then build a separate secure three-node cluster with users, ACLs, quotas, and production topics. Finally, change parameters, connect clients, verify monitoring, and perform pre-launch checks.

Tutorial Scope

Start before deploying Kafka. You need a working Pigsty administration node with INFRA installed. Otherwise, complete quick installation first. Target nodes need SSH/sudo access and must be manageable by NODE.

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
KAFKA uses 15 persistent public parameters. The role derives topology, listeners, storage subdirectories, replication safety, authorization, and exporter placement consistently. Start with Quickstart. See Parameters for the field reference.

Plan First, Then Format

kafka_seq becomes KRaft node.id. A new cluster’s bootstrap manifest freezes the random Cluster ID, initial controller identities, security profile, and initial replication policy. After formatting, do not casually change identities, security profile, or controllers. The role checks live state against the manifest and blocks conflicts. It never silently overwrites or reformats data.

item.title: Parameters
item.description:
KAFKA exposes 15 persistent parameters. The role derives topology, listeners, security, storage subdirectories, replication safety, and exporter placement consistently. Additional persistent variables cannot override these derived settings.

Parameter Overview

Parameter Level Default Description
kafka_cluster Cluster required Kafka cluster identity
kafka_seq Instance required Cluster-unique KRaft node.id
kafka_role Instance combined combined, broker, or controller
kafka_cluster_id Cluster unset Takeover/recovery assertion; randomly generated for a new cluster
kafka_data Instance /data/kafka Role-owned data root directory
kafka_heap_opts Instance -Xms1G -Xmx1G Kafka JVM heap
kafka_port Instance 9092 Broker/client port
kafka_controller_port Instance 9093 KRaft controller port
kafka_rack Instance unset Broker fault-domain label
kafka_parameters Cluster/Instance {} Non-role-owned broker parameters
kafka_jmx_exporter_port Instance 9404 JMX Exporter HTTP port
kafka_exporter_port Instance 9308 Protocol Exporter HTTP port
kafka_security Cluster plaintext plaintext or the production scram profile
kafka_users Cluster [] User credentials, ACLs, and quotas
kafka_topics Cluster [] Declarative topics

Set kafka_cluster and kafka_seq. kafka_role has a default. Omit it on every member or declare it on every member.

item.title: Administration
item.description:
KAFKA installs Kafka in /opt/kafka and manages it with Systemd. Declare persistent settings in pigsty.yml. Do not edit generated node files manually.

These CLI examples use the generated /etc/kafka/admin.properties. Keep --command-config even with plaintext. Commands then retain the same structure if the administration channel changes to scram. Replace <broker>:9092 with a reachable inventory_hostname and port.

–command-config on the console tools requires a Kafka 4.2+ CLI

Starting with Kafka 4.2, KIP-1147 standardized --command-config for files and --command-property for key-value arguments across all CLIs. /opt/kafka/bin comes from the Pigsty repository, currently with a 4.3.x payload. It supports these examples. External 4.1 or older console tools require --producer.config and --consumer.config. Administration tools such as kafka-topics.sh, kafka-configs.sh, kafka-acls.sh, kafka-consumer-groups.sh, and kafka-metadata-quorum.sh already used --command-config. They are unaffected.

item.title: Playbook
item.description:
kafka.yml deploys Apache Kafka 4.1+ dynamic KRaft and applies security, resources, and monitoring. kafka-rm.yml removes members or tears down clusters.

Cluster Completeness Constraint

Each selected kafka_cluster must include every member. Partial selection fails before writes. One cluster, several complete clusters, and a bare whole-inventory run are permitted. First run --check against the identical target. Before execution, manually verify backup or rebuild intent, capacity, business window, rollback, and change approval.

item.title: Monitoring
item.description:
Kafka monitoring combines metrics, logs, dashboards, and alerts. It covers JVM internals and the Kafka protocol view. You can inspect partitions, ISR, and consumer lag together with JVM state, request queues, and KRaft controller health.

Scrape Architecture

The KAFKA module uses two complementary exporters:

Scrape Surface Service / Method Job Node Scope Main Content
JVM and Kafka internals JMX Exporter Java agent :9404 kafka (with role label) All Kafka nodes JVM, broker throughput, replication, request path, KRaft, controller
Kafka protocol view kafka_exporter :9308 kafka (no role label) The one or two broker-capable nodes with the smallest kafka_seq Broker, topic, partition, offset, consumer group, lag
Host resources node_exporter node Managed nodes CPU, memory, disk, network, filesystem
Logs Journald → Vector → VictoriaLogs syslog All Kafka nodes Structured, searchable Kafka and exporter logs

On each INFRA node, the role creates one discovery file per instance. JMX and any selected protocol target share that file and kafka scrape job:

item.title: Metrics
item.description:
Both metric sources use job=kafka. JMX targets have a role label and collect each JVM’s internal state. Protocol targets lack role and collect logical cluster, topic, partition, and consumer-group state through Kafka protocol. Protocol exporters run on the one or two broker-capable nodes with the lowest kafka_seq. Single-broker clusters run one.

JMX uses an allowlist for standard JVM and selected broker, replication, request-path, and KRaft metrics. It excludes per-client and per-partition MBeans to limit series counts. Protocol exporters provide partition details.

item.title: FAQ
item.description:
How mature is the current KAFKA module?

The v1 baseline provides dynamic KRaft, full-cluster checks, cold start and repair, serial broker admission, and dynamic controller join. It supports retirement of live or dead members and three-command failed-node replacement. It also provides strict rolling restarts, TLS/SCRAM/ACL, declared topics and users, protected credential and certificate rotation, and complete monitoring.

Production requires kafka_security: scram, an odd controller count, and sufficient brokers, RF, and minISR. You must plan capacity, reassignment, balancing, upgrades, backup, restore, and failure exercises. This module does not provide a managed Kafka service. Default plaintext suits only development or trusted isolated networks.
